newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine TV airs Menem probe after censorship row.
newsitem.headline: Argentine TV airs Menem probe after censorship row.

text.p: An Argentine television channel which refused to air an investigation into President Carlos Menem's home town said on Friday it had changed its mind and broadcast the show to head off a censorship row.

A spokesman for the America TV group said America 2 and a cable channel began airing the show late Thursday because of a fierce debate which forced Peronist chief Menem to go on the radio to deny his government had leant on the broadcasters.
"My government has never put pressure on anybody to make them change the thrust of their programmes, information or commentaries," Menem told National Radio.

He dismissed as absurd the investigation by journalist Roman Lejtman, an outspoken critic of the Peronist government, into his grandiose building projects in his home town of Anillaco, in the northwest desert province La Rioja.

The programme asked questions about who paid for Menem's huge pink ranch-style home in Anillaco, his nearby mountain refuge with a heliport and an artificial lake for fishing, a brand-new full-length runway in the desert built by the air force -- for a town of just 850 -- and a zoo.
"It is absurd to try to tarnish the image, honesty and morality of the president with this sort of thing," said the 67-year-old Peronist leader.

"If the president of the nation after so many years' work and struggle cannot build himself a house, which is not small but is austere, in the town where he was born, what country are we living in?" he asked. Aides say he has been building it for 12 years, since before becoming president in 1989.

But Argentina's two main opposition parties, the Radicals and centre-left Frepaso, demanded on Friday that Menem explain the financing of the Anillaco projects. The Frepaso said it would send parliamentarians to La Rioja to interiew local officials.
"We need a full account of who ordered and who financed these projects and what is their sense and rationale," said Radical leader Rodolfo Terrango.
Lejtman said on his Friday radio show he was relieved that the America media group's owner, Eduardo Eurnekian, "showed he was an intelligent man" by deciding not to censor the show.
America had suspended the show, originally scheduled for Wednesday night, saying the investigation "had to be analysed in case its airing causes the channel legal problems."
The journalists accused Menem's press office of leaning on America in a "serious case of censorship" -- prompting a quick government offer to broadcast the show on state channel ATC.
Journalists and politicians said the episode raised fears for freedom of the press already running high after the murder of a photographer for Noticias news magazine one month ago.
